data_output.description: data.py must preserve the existing encoded tuple structure (features, labels, users) and canonical split row order. Each feature matrix must have four columns: encoded user id (int32), encoded video id (int32), prior-user exponentially decayed positive long_view count (float32), and prior-user exponentially decayed negative long_view count (float32). For every row, both history values must exclude the current impression and all later impressions. Validation processing may use labels from preceding training events, but must not use any validation label before that row's features are generated. Unknown users and videos retain the existing vocabulary behavior. The fixed command must write predictions_valid.npz containing exactly row_ids and scores, with row_ids equal to canonical validation positions in order and scores of identical length; no ground-truth array may be written or loaded by training for evaluation.

model_input.description: model.py must accept four-column features while remaining compatible with the existing Model interface: logits(features), step(features, labels), predict(features), state(), and load_state(). The first two columns index user and item parameters; the final two columns are continuous history features. The logit must add two separately learned scalar coefficients, one multiplying the decayed prior-positive count and one multiplying the decayed prior-negative count, to the existing additive user/item effects and low-rank interaction. Both coefficients must participate in optimization, L2 regularization, checkpoint state, and restoration. train.py must retain the existing pointwise long_view loss, training split, within_user_auc checkpoint proxy, and patience behavior.
